narrative: 我们在看到隔壁房间之前先听到了它（J-cut）：画面还停留在走路的人身上，声音却已经先到了。或者，当说话者的话音仍在继续时，我们看到的是倾听者（L-cut）：这张脸成了衔接的桥梁。
声音会提前或滞后。这张脸就是那座桥。
当画面和音轨不应该在同一帧上剪辑，以便让思绪能够跨越一道门槛时使用它。当你需要同时看到两个房间时（分屏，Split Screen），或者当你只需要一个没有重叠音轨的哑巴反应镜头时，这个手法就用错了。
随意错位的音乐并不自动构成有意义的对位。要明确这种滞后揭示的是什么：恐惧、讽刺，还是一种不愿放开那张脸的声音。
how: 在时间线上，J-cut让即将到来的音频在即将离开的画面下方就开始播放。L-cut则让即将离开的音频在即将到来的画面下方继续。
这里所说的“画面设定”是指一个能够承受这种重叠的镜头：一个反应镜头（Reaction Shot）、一次走向门口的动作、一间空荡的办公室。让声音的来源保持足够清晰，使这种重叠成为一种信息，而不是含混。
提示词：a frame of [Subject] designed as the picture half of an L-cut or J-cut, reaction holding while another space is already speaking.
when: 用它来在房间出现之前先进入一段对话，在一次坦白之后依然停留在倾听者身上，或者让一首歌在一场与它无关的打包行李戏上继续播放。如果两张脸应该分享同样的同期对白，就不要把它当作默认的对话剪辑方式。
如果你需要的是“与此同时”式的地理关系，就用交叉剪辑（Cross-Cutting）。
vs: 反应镜头是画面本身；J-cut和L-cut则是这幅画面与声音相遇的方式。交叉剪辑交替呈现的是完整的段落。
画面剪辑点上声音的猛然一撞，更接近硬切（Smash Cut）。对位手法（欢快的音乐配上残酷的画面）可以借助L-cut来实现，但这里说的技法是错位的拼接方式本身，而不是选曲这件事。
examples_film: 《社交网络》（The Social Network）和《盗火线》（Heat）让台词持续覆盖在倾听者的脸上，让思绪跨越剪接点继续存在。《窃听大阴谋》（The Conversation）让传入的声音在画面解释之前就成为一种威胁。
《一一》（Yi Yi）让钢琴声先于其来源出现。《发条橙》（A Clockwork Orange）和《落水狗》（Reservoir Dogs）把欢快的曲子放在画面并不认可的行为之上。
用这种错位手法，而不是照搬那种“金曲空降”式的用法。
mistakes: 最常见的误用近亲是画面和声音同步剪辑的哑巴反应镜头，或者从不重叠音轨的交叉剪辑。破绽是：在画面剪辑点处，新房间里的嘴唇已经同步说着话，没有任何“预先叠入”的迹象。
解决办法是：让第一幅画面保持，同时第二条音轨已经开始；或者让第一条音轨在画面已经切换之后继续保留。

faq.q: 电影中的“声画错位剪辑（J-Cut / L-Cut）”是什么？
faq.a: J-cut让下一个镜头的声音先于其画面出现；L-cut让上一个镜头的声音在画面已经切换之后继续存在。这里的“画面设定”指的是一个能够在另一个空间发声时依然维持住的画面。

faq.q: 声画错位剪辑 vs 反应镜头
faq.a: 反应镜头是一幅关于倾听的画面。J-cut和L-cut则是这幅画面与另一个空间的声音相衔接的方式。你完全可以用一次直接剪辑来呈现反应镜头；J/L手法指的正是那种错位。

faq.q: 什么时候该用声画错位剪辑？
faq.a: 当声音应该先于画面把观众带入一场戏，或者在我们已经离开之后依然萦绕不去时使用。当画面和音轨必须同时撞击才对时，不要用它。

faq.q: 如何为AI图像或视频撰写声画错位剪辑的提示词？
faq.a: 描述一张能够承载画外声音的脸或房间。示例：A frame of [Subject] as the picture half of an L-cut or J-cut, reaction holding while another space is already speaking. 视频的话，要说明哪条音轨是预先叠入的。

narrative: We hear the next room before we see it (J-cut): the picture stays on the walker, the voice has already arrived. Or we see the listener while the speaker's words continue (L-cut): the face is the bridge.
Sound will lead or lag. The face is the bridge.

Use it when picture and track should not cut on the same frame, so thought can cross a doorway. It is the wrong tool when you need both rooms visible at once (Split Screen) or when you only need a mute reaction insert with no overlapping track.
Randomly mismatched music is not automatically meaningful counterpoint. Define what the lag reveals: dread, irony, a voice that will not let the face go.
how: On the timeline, a J-cut lets incoming audio start under the outgoing picture. An L-cut lets outgoing audio continue under the incoming picture.
The visual setup is a shot that can bear that overlap: a Reaction Shot, a walk toward a door, an empty office. Keep the sound's source clear enough that the overlap is information, not muddle.
Prompt: a frame of [Subject] designed as the picture half of an L-cut or J-cut, reaction holding while another space is already speaking.
when: Use it to enter a conversation before the room, to stay on a listener after a confession, to let a song continue over a packing scene it does not belong to. Do not use it as default dialogue cutting if both faces should share the same on-camera words.
If you need meanwhile geography, Cross-Cutting.
vs: A Reaction Shot is the picture; J-cut and L-cut are how that picture meets sound. Cross-Cutting alternates whole lines.
A smash in sound on a picture cut is closer to Smash Cut. Counterpoint (cheerful music on a cruel image) can ride an L-cut, but the technique here is the staggered splice, not the playlist.
examples_film: The Social Network and Heat keep speech living over listeners' faces so thought continues across the join. The Conversation makes incoming sound a threat before the picture explains it.
Yi Yi lets piano arrive before its source is located. A Clockwork Orange and Reservoir Dogs place cheerful tracks against behavior the picture will not bless.
Use the stagger, not the needle-drop.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a mute Reaction Shot with picture and sound cutting together, or a Cross-Cutting that never overlaps track. The tell: lips in the new room are already talking in sync at the picture cut, with no pre-lap.
The fix: hold the first picture while the second track starts, or hold the first track after the picture has moved.

faq.q: What is J-Cut / L-Cut (Visual Setup) in film?
faq.a: A J-cut starts the next shot's sound before its picture; an L-cut keeps the last shot's sound after the picture has changed. The visual setup is a frame that can hold while the other space speaks.
A reaction shot is a picture of listening. J-cut and L-cut are how that picture is joined to another space's sound. You can have a reaction with a straight cut; the J/L is the stagger.

faq.q: When should I use J-Cut / L-Cut (Visual Setup)?
faq.a: Use it when sound should lead a scene in, or linger after we have left. Do not use it if picture and track must hit together as a smash.

faq.q: How do I prompt J-Cut / L-Cut (Visual Setup) for AI image or video?
faq.a: Describe a face or room that can hold offscreen voice. Example: A frame of [Subject] as the picture half of an L-cut or J-cut, reaction holding while another space is already speaking. For video, say which track pre-laps.
